Bayes Studio, a Vancouver-based startup, develops AI-driven wildfire detection systems using edge-deployed camera devices. Their existing workflow—consisting of manual labeling, model training, and compression—limited their ability to update detection models quickly as new image data became available. This project addresses that bottleneck by developing an automated and modular pipeline for end-to-end model improvement.

The pipeline is designed to process incoming data through a semi-automated labeling system that combines predictions from two models (YOLOv8 and Grounding DINO) with human-in-the-loop validation for uncertain cases. Labeled images then undergo data augmentation to increase dataset diversity. The pipeline fine-tunes a YOLOv8 base model on this expanded dataset and applies knowledge distillation and quantization to produce smaller, deployable models for edge devices.

Key outputs include a labeled dataset, fine-tuned and compressed models, and versioned metadata to support traceability and reproducibility. While the system currently runs locally, it provides a foundation for scalable wildfire detection workflows. Limitations such as lack of cloud support, fragmented metadata storage, and missing monitoring tools are acknowledged, with recommendations proposed to address them.

Overall, this solution helps the partner streamline model updates and prepare models suitable for real-time edge deployment in wildfire detection.
